critical_code_review_comments: routers/phase9._run_due_callbacks: when Twilio creds exist it DOES NOT guard against being called twice for the same job between the time the Twilio call is placed and the followup_jobs status update; a slow DB write could cause a duplicate dial on a retried cron. Consider updating status to 'sending' with a conditional update BEFORE calling Twilio (compare-and-set on status='scheduled').

routers/phase9.handle_confirmation_reply only inspects the next 48h window and picks the earliest appt. If a customer has two upcoming appts, replying 'YES' always confirms the sooner one — fine for most cases but if the earlier is already confirmed and the later is pending, YES silently reconfirms the first. Consider skipping already-confirmed appts when the reply is unambiguous.

routers/phase9.service_area_heatmap geocodes top ZIPs sequentially inside the request path with a 10s timeout each × 12 — that is up to 120s added latency on a cold cache. Move geocode fan-out to asyncio.gather with a semaphore of 3-4, or do it lazily in a background job and persist lat/lon on the bucket.

routers/phase9.schedule_review_request_2h uses db.followup_jobs.update_one with upsert and $set that always rewrites 'id' and 'created_at'. On re-trigger (status flipped completed→scheduled→completed) you'll keep the same (tenant_id, appointment_id, kind) doc but mutate id and created_at — this breaks any downstream reference by id. Use $setOnInsert for id/created_at and $set for send_at/body only.

routers/phase9.standup_ics does not include a VTIMEZONE and uses the current moment as DTSTART; most calendar clients will render it as 'now' instead of a planned morning slot. Consider pinning DTSTART to 08:00 local or using the business's working hours.

routers/cron.cron_callbacks_due + cron_appt_confirmations ack 2xx and fire asyncio.create_task — if the worker is restarted mid-cron the batch is lost. Consider persisting a cron_runs row with status so retries can detect in-progress work (same comment made in iteration 7 for daily-standup; still unaddressed).
